title: What Happens to Gift Card Balances Nobody Spends
title_alternates: The Money Left on Gift Cards and Who Ends Up With It
Unspent Gift Card Balances and What the Law Does With Them
description:
There is a gift card in your house with money still on it. Not the whole balance, just the awkward part you never went back for. That leftover has a name inside the company that sold it, and in some states it does not belong to them at all.

This episode explains what breakage is, why an unspent balance is booked as income rather than treated as a loss, and how federal law protects the funds from expiring without ever sending them back to you. You will see why two states can reach opposite answers on the same balance, and which rule decides. You will also see how to search the official state databases for money held in your name, for free, and what people get wrong when they search. Every figure is sourced to an official filing, statute or agency page.

If you have found money in a state database, say which state in the comments, it helps other people know where to look.

Chapters
00:00 The card in the drawer
00:45 Breakage, and why it is income
02:15 How a balance becomes unclaimed
03:00 What federal law actually protects
04:00 The scale of it
05:00 Unclaimed property law and escheat
06:30 Which state's rule applies
07:00 How to check your own name
08:30 Cash back on small balances
09:00 What to prepare

Official resources mentioned in this video:
MissingMoney.com, the multi-state unclaimed property search: https://www.missingmoney.com/
NAUPA, directory of every state unclaimed property program: https://unclaimed.org/
USA.gov, federal unclaimed money resources: https://www.usa.gov/unclaimed-money
CFPB, federal gift card rules under Regulation E: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/regulations/1005/20/
New York Abandoned Property Law section 1315: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/ABP/1315
California Civil Code section 1749.5, cash redemption: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1749.5
California Code of Civil Procedure section 1520.5, gift certificate exemption: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CCP&sectionNum=1520.5
Washington RCW 19.240.020, cash redemption: https://app.leg.wa.gov/rcw/default.aspx?cite=19.240.020
Connecticut OLR 2023-R-0195, gift card cash back laws by state: https://www.cga.ct.gov/2023/rpt/pdf/2023-R-0195.pdf
Starbucks Form 10-K, fiscal 2025: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/829224/000082922425000114/sbux-20250928.htm

This video is general information about US programmes, rules and databases. It is not legal, tax, insurance or financial advice, and it does not create any professional relationship. Rules and deadlines vary by state and change over time. Always verify your own situation directly with the official source or administrator named above, or with a qualified professional. We do not charge for information about how to claim money, and neither do the official databases mentioned here.
